the output waves for a volume grating replayed at the perfect Bragg angle and index matched to the surroundings are accurately approximated by the following analytic formulas: (1) the forward-propagating wave is proportional to the Fourier transform of the grating profile and (2) the backward-propagating wave, which is the most important for practical applications, is proportional to the sum of two terms.

the output waves of a volume grating can be calculated in closed form in terms of boundary-diffraction-coefficient (BDC) expressions, which are the same as those for the surface gratings, but the coefficients must be computed for a volume-grating profile that has the grating slant angle included in the profile shape.

a new approximate analytic method for the calculation of the diffraction of an electromagnetic wave by a volume grating.
the development of a new analytic method that permits the calculation, in a relatively straightforward way, of the diffraction properties of volume gratings, both slanted and normal to the surface.
the study of diffraction by volume gratins, in the framework of the rigorous coupled-wave analysis (RCWA) and the boundary diffraction coefficient method (BDCM).

the approximate analytic solution presented is accurate and efficient for a large range of volume grating parameters and can be used as a first-order approximation to the rigorous coupled-wave solution.

the method presented here is a powerful, simple, and accurate analytic technique that can be used to calculate the diffraction efficiency and the angular distribution of the diffracted waves from a wide range of gratings.
the present theory is accurate to the order of the permettivity variation of the grating and that the second-order terms are negligible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the analytic expressions for the output waves are valid for a large class of volume gratings.

the analytic solution is valid for all values of the grating thickness, and for all values of its slanting angle, provided that its permittivity is not too far from unity and its permittivity variation is not too strong, and that the replay angle is the Bragg angle.
the approximate analytic expressions presented here provide an accurate, simple, and efficient tool for calculating the diffraction by volume grattings.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a simple analytic expression for the boundary diffraction coefficients can be obtained in terms of the volume gratings' permittivity profile, which permits a straightforward calculation of the output waves for any volume grating, regardless of the grating geometry.
the boundary diffraction coefficients of a volume grating are not the same as those of the corresponding surface grating.

the diffraction of a plane wave by a volume grating can be reduced to the diffraction of the incident plane wave by an equivalent boundary grating that has a periodic modulation in the normal direction of the grating planes.
